strings.name: Caetano Veloso
strings.summary: Born in Bahia, Veloso helped shape Tropicália alongside Gilberto Gil, Gal Costa and others, combining Brazilian traditions, rock and experimental art. Detained under military rule and exiled in London, he returned in 1972 and continued exploring identity, modernity and social life through music. His influence spans the Portuguese-speaking world and international audiences. In 2026 he shared the Global Music Album Grammy with his sister Maria Bethânia.

strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and beginnings
strings.facts.f2.value: Completed secondary school in Salvador and studied philosophy, drawing early influence from Brazilian music, cinema and theater.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Helping shape Tropicália
strings.highlights.h1.text: Joined artists combining Brazilian popular traditions, rock and avant-garde expression in the 1960s.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Music across generations and borders
strings.highlights.h2.text: Continued recording and performing, sharing a 2026 Global Music Album Grammy with Maria Bethânia.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Shared Global Music Album Grammy
strings.timeline.t1.text: Won with Maria Bethânia for Caetano e Bethânia Ao Vivo.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Released Meu Coco
strings.timeline.t2.text: An original studio album continued explorations of Brazilian society, memory and musical language.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Honored by Latin Recording Academy
strings.timeline.t3.text: Named Person of the Year for his long musical contribution.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Released Livro
strings.timeline.t4.text: The album combining literature, arrangements and Brazilian music later earned Grammy recognition.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Returned from London exile
strings.timeline.t5.text: Returned to Brazil and released Transa, continuing a cross-cultural musical language.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Went into exile in London
strings.timeline.t6.text: After detention and restrictions under military rule, left Brazil and continued creating in Britain with Gil.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joined Tropicália collective album
strings.timeline.t7.text: Participated in Tropicália: ou Panis et Circencis; was detained by the military regime later that year.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Released first collaborative album
strings.timeline.t8.text: Recorded Domingo with Gal Costa and gained further attention through festival performances.
